newsitem.title: USA: A mother says military must prevent inquiry suicides.
newsitem.headline: A mother says military must prevent inquiry suicides.

text.p: A mother said Tuesday a Navy hazing investigation apparently drove her son to suicide and the military must act to assure a newly disclosed Marine hazing incident does not cause more suicides.

Mary O'Brien, of Media, Pennsylvania, said her son Dennis apparently shot himself to death on his submarine in 1995 because of pressure by higher ups and investigators to identify sailors who hazed him.

She said she fears a videotape made public two weeks ago of Marines pounding medals into young paratroopers' chests will spur investigations causing more suicides unless the military sets guidelines to prevent it.
"What we are deathly afraid of is a major reaction to that videotape," she said. "We are so afraid ... they are going to make an example of someone and some other parent is going to lose a child."
Mrs. O'Brien and her husband, Dennis O'Brien Sr., spoke at a press conference arranged by their congressman, Representative Curt Weldon, a Pennsylvania Republican.

Weldon said he intended to press Defence Secretary William Cohen at a hearing Wednesday to establish guidelines to protect servicemen from undue pressure in hazing investigations, and to help the O'Briens get more information on what happened to their son.
The O'Briens said the hazing of their son was not nearly as serious as that in the videotape in which Marines were shown pounding sharp medals into new paratroopers so hard that some collapsed.

The O'Briens said their son Dennis was awarded his Dolphins pin, making him a fully qualified submariner, Oct. 13, 1995, and fellow sailors put him through a ritual in which they hit the medal hard enough to leave a bruise.

But they said the top enlisted man on the submarine, backed by a top submarine commander in the Pacific, ordered a heavy handed criminal investigation and that it led to the full crew being confined to the submarine.
Under the pressure, they said, their son apparently shot himself to death while standing watch two weeks later. They said they were not certain he was not shot by someone else.
